summary.headline: Thomas Cook (India) Q4 FY26 group revenue fell 10% YoY to INR 17,707 million as Middle East war hit DEI and Desert Adventures, while Sterling and India operations grew.
summary.overview: Management framed FY26 in two phases: the first nine months were relatively stable (top line up 7%, EBITDA up marginally), while Q4 absorbed the Middle East conflict, airfare spikes and rupee weakness, with the Pahalgam/Operation Sindoor disruption earlier in the year. Full-year consolidated income rose 3% to INR 83,982 million (INR 85,578 million per closing remarks), but EBT fell 14% to INR 3,268 million. India operations grew EBT 16% in Q4, and Sterling posted record Q4 numbers. The board approved in-principle demerger of the resort business into Sterling Holiday Resorts, with a timeline of Q1 FY28.

segments.name: Financial Services (Forex, Education, Remittance)
segments.commentary: Q4 forex revenue +3% to INR 813 million with EBIT +17% to INR 392 million (48% margin); FY26 flat at INR 3,261 million revenue and INR 1,493 million EBIT. Prepaid card float about INR 16 billion on USD 764 million load volume; card now covers 28 currencies.

segments.name: Travel & Related Services (B2C)
segments.commentary: B2C is about 27% of travel portfolio and grew 8% in FY26 and in Q4; short-haul bookings +17% for FY and +21% in Q4, while long-haul remained subdued.

segments.name: Travel & Related Services (B2B)
segments.commentary: B2B (about 73% of travel revenue) grew 2% in FY26 but fell 18% in Q4; international DMS revenue +3% in FY and -24% in Q4, with Desert Adventures down 50% in Q4.

segments.name: MICE
segments.commentary: Q4 MICE revenue fell 2% due to about INR 100 crore of government MICE business and about INR 100 crore of Desert Adventures MICE absent from last year; corporate MICE grew 21% in Q4 and 6% for FY26.

segments.name: Corporate Travel
segments.commentary: FY26 turnover INR 27 billion (net basis) and revenue INR 1,541 million, +19% YoY; Q4 revenue +28%. Air volume +7.3% in Q4 and +4.8% for FY26.

segments.name: Sterling Holiday Resorts
segments.commentary: 78 resorts with about 3,800 rooms across 65 destinations; Q4 occupancy 64%, ARR +12% to INR 6,347, RevPAR +16%. Cash about INR 3,400 million and debt-free.

segments.name: DEI (Digiphoto)
segments.commentary: About 50% of revenue from UAE; Q4 revenue INR 194 crore and EBIT negative INR 10 crore. Far East and APAC grew, and management expects Middle East recovery of 50-60% by year-end.

guidance_outlook: Travel EBIT margin objective of about 5% is maintained per management, though it depends on DMS units becoming profitable and short-haul mix could mechanically lower the margin.
Sterling expects to cross 95 resorts and 4,500 rooms in 2027, with more than 20 sign-ups in pipeline; Q1 FY27 described as having no headwinds so far; EBITDA margin range of 32-35% cited as stable.
DEI expects Middle East recovery of about 50-60% by year-end; management said FY26 will not deliver what was originally planned for DEI.
Demerger of resort business into Sterling Holiday Resorts expected to complete by Q1 FY28, per the 12-15 month plan; applications filed with NSE and BSE.
Board recommended dividend of INR 0.50 to INR 1 per share, subject to shareholder approval.
Management expects MICE deferred demand to return in Q2 and Q3 FY27 rather than being lost.
capex_capacity: Sterling: 78 resorts and about 3,800 rooms, with 62% P&L-led and 38% managed inventory; about 14 resorts added in FY26; three land banks available for greenfield development.
Sterling: monsoon asset-protection spends planned to be completed by mid-June.
Group: increasing technology capex for software and automation; part of net cash to repay long-term loans with fixed schedules over the next couple of years.
DEI: WeC software fully live for 2 months; cost actions on people, IT services via AI, third-party licences and property costs.
Forex: 1,100 corporate clients, about 800 corporate travel relationships, and 800+ education counsellors; digital penetration 23%.
demand_pricing: Q4 long-haul forward bookings weak, especially Europe and parts of eastbound; UAE and CIS volumes dropped completely; westbound airfares up 30-50%.
Short-haul (China, Vietnam, Cambodia, Japan) remains the preferred choice on double-digit growth; long-haul ticket sizes are larger, so short-haul does not fully offset lost volume.
Management is using tactical pricing and cash-back offers, which pressure margins temporarily.
Education forex gained share despite the LRS decline (education LRS -22% vs TCIL +17%); travel LRS -3% vs TCIL holiday forex +13%.
Retail forex margin about 2.0-2.2% and wholesale about 0.6-0.7%, which management says are unchanged.
RBI notification lets AD2 entities handle capital-account trade remittances up to INR 25 lakh per transaction; RBI will not issue new FFMC licences.

qa_highlights.question: Why did financial services top line and EBIT drop, and is margin being traded for share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 forex EBIT rose 17% and FY EBIT held at about INR 149 crore; the drop reflects mix shift and net revenue reporting with franchise revenue shares, not margin pressure. Float of about INR 16 billion was flat vs December, which management read as customers not spending.

qa_highlights.question: Why has Sterling EBIT been flat at about INR 129 crore for two years despite rising room count?
qa_highlights.answer: Vikram Lalvani cited the end of membership acquisition revenue, a 2-3 month ramp-up lag for new resorts, and upfront costs. Krishna Kumar cited high ROU depreciation from leased resorts. EBITDA margin was 31% and EBIT margin 24%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the DEI loss behind us and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Ram said the corrections are not done and the cost base will reduce over 30-60 days notice periods. He expects Middle East recovery of 50-60% by year-end and said FY26 will not match original plans. Debasis Nandy said top line depends on ground conditions.

qa_highlights.question: Net cash and deployment plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Debasis Nandy said net cash is close to INR 800 crore, to be used for technology capex, repayment of long-term loans over the next couple of years, and inorganic growth if returns criteria are met. An analyst's build-up gave about INR 730-740 crore, which was confirmed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q1 outlook for Sterling and monsoon risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Vikram Lalvani said there are no headwinds so far in Q1; occupancy is expected to rise toward 65-70% over the year. Monsoon risk is being managed by asset protection and a geographically spread portfolio, with Q3 now the strongest quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the demerger timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Debasis Nandy said the process is on track for the 12-15 month plan, applications are with NSE and BSE, and completion is expected by Q1 FY28.

risks_watch: Middle East conflict and westbound long-haul demand; DEI recovery pace (50-60% expected by year-end) and cost reset timing.
Travel EBIT margin trajectory toward 5% as short-haul mix rises and DMS units remain loss-making.
Forward booking softness and MICE deferral into Q2-Q3 FY27.
Demerger approvals from NSE and BSE and completion by Q1 FY28.
Sterling monsoon and weather impact on Q2, and EBIT conversion from new resorts given ROU depreciation.
Impact of RBI's revised AD norms and the planned AD3 category on the forex business.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the India and Sterling operations and on structural positives, but cautious on the outlook. Management was candid that Q4 and FY26 were hit by geopolitical events, and several answers on DEI and long-haul were hedged with timing uncertainty.
key_quotes: While the environment remains uncertain, we are cautiously optimistic that these will endure.
Sterling is now just not growing faster: it is growing better with greater predictability, stronger operating leverage, increasing cash generation and disciplined capital allocation.
There is no dearth of pipeline in terms of inquiries that are coming from our customers.
So, the corrections have been done.
We expect this process to get completed by Q1 of FY '28, which was the original timeline that we had intimated.

adds.what: Sterling Holiday Resorts: expects to cross 95 resorts and 4,500 rooms in 2027 (from 78 resorts, ~3,800 rooms), with 20+ sign-ups in pipeline

growth.why: Q4 group revenue fell 10% YoY on Middle East war and B2B weakness, with management guiding only to a 5% travel EBIT margin objective held, Sterling expanding to 95+ resorts and 4,500 rooms in 2027 backed by a pipeline of 20+ sign-ups, and DEI Middle East recovery of 50-60% by year-end.
